stages.description: Parameterize both string-formatted SQL statements in records/routes.py: create_note's INSERT and search_notes' LIKE query, matching the pattern used correctly elsewhere in the codebase.
acceptance_criteria: test_add_note_with_apostrophe_breaks_current_implementation and test_search_with_apostrophe_breaks_current_implementation both flip from pytest.raises(sqlite3.OperationalError) to a normal successful call that stores/finds the apostrophe literally - update both tests as part of this stage.
No route in records/routes.py builds a SQL string via % formatting or f-strings against request data.

stages.description: Add an audit trail: every add_note and search_notes call writes a row to a new audit_log table (who/what/when - requester identity if the caller supplies one, action type, patient_id touched, timestamp), addressing the 'no audit trail despite PHI access' finding. Does not add access control itself (see backlog) - only makes access observable after the fact.
acceptance_criteria: All existing records tests still pass.
New test: after calling add_note and search_notes, the audit_log table has one row per call with the correct action type and patient_id/query recorded.
Audit log writes never block or fail the underlying operation - a logging failure must not turn a successful note-add into an error response.

stages.description: Stop returning ssn/dob by default from GET /patients/<id> and GET /patients. Default response includes only id/name/phone; ssn and dob are only included when the caller passes ?include_sensitive=true. This does not add real authorization (there's no auth model to hook into yet - see backlog) but removes PII from the default, most-likely-to-be-called path.
acceptance_criteria: test_register_creates_patient and test_get_patient_unknown still pass unmodified.

test_get_patient_returns_full_record_including_ssn is renamed/split: a new default-request assertion that ssn/dob are ABSENT, plus a new test that ?include_sensitive=true still returns them - this is a deliberate, flagged behavior change to the default response shape, not a pure refactor.
test_list_patients_returns_everyone_no_filtering still passes on count, but its per-patient assertions must not check for ssn/dob in the default response.

stages.description: Remove the plaintext PII from register_patient's debug print() - log only that a registration occurred and the resulting patient id, never the payload contents.
acceptance_criteria: All existing patients tests still pass.
grep confirms no print() or log call in patients/routes.py includes the raw request payload, ssn, or dob.
A new test captures stdout/log output during register_patient and asserts the SSN value used in the test does not appear in it.

stages.description: Reject scheduling an appointment when the same provider already has one at the same scheduled_at, instead of silently double-booking.
acceptance_criteria: test_schedule_appointment and test_list_appointments_for_patient still pass unmodified.

test_double_booking_same_provider_same_slot_is_not_rejected's expectation flips: the second request for the same provider/slot now returns 409 (or 400) instead of 201 - update and rename the test as part of this stage.
Scheduling the same provider at a different scheduled_at, or a different provider at the same scheduled_at, still succeeds - only the exact (provider, scheduled_at) collision is rejected.
